intro: One real diagnosis code a day, straight from the official ICD-10-CM code set, with a deadpan note from a coder who has seen too much. The codes and descriptions are real. The notes are satire.

source.name: ICD-10-CM
source.publisher: CDC National Center for Health Statistics

entries.note: Please confirm the duck was in network.
Follow-up visit. The duck has not returned our calls.
Sequela: the late effects. The duck remains at large. The deductible has reset.
A coder must now decide between a bite and a strike. Nobody has asked the duck.
Geese have their own code because someone, somewhere, watched a goose and took notes.
Wait time for the appointment: see Z75.2.
Not to be confused with struck by chicken. The classification is firm on this.
The chicken’s side of the story is not a required field.
Seasonal, like open enrollment, and about as welcome.
The parrot repeats what the coder said about the payer. Not billable.

entries.description: Struck by other psittacines, initial encounter
entries.note: The cockatoo, the budgie and every other parrot-adjacent bird share one code. Macaws got their own.

entries.description: Other contact with other birds, initial encounter
entries.note: The classification’s way of saying: a bird did something.
The rabies question triggers four forms. The squirrel signs none.
The smallest rodent with its own code, and a claim larger than the mouse.
Mice and rats are coded separately. The rodents were not consulted.
A staple of the emergency department, and still no code for: it was a good dog.
Bites and scratches are coded separately. The cat considers this an overreach.
The cat has declined to be attached to the chart.
Please indicate the number of horsepower. It is, as a rule, one.
Cows cannot be sued. Their insurers, however, are well represented.

entries.description: Bitten by other hoof stock, initial encounter
entries.note: Please identify the species. Species identification is not a covered service.
Pigs have their own code. The pig did not ask for it.
The raccoon has taken the chart and left.
Yes, dolphins have a code. No, the dolphin does not have a payer.
Orcas are dolphins, but the classification lists them separately. Coders have opinions.
Slow, but still faster than a prior authorization.

entries.description: Bitten by nonvenomous lizards, initial encounter
entries.note: ‘Nonvenomous’ is a determination usually made after the copay.

entries.description: Contact with nonvenomous frogs, initial encounter
entries.note: Kissing is billed separately.

entries.description: Contact with nonvenomous toads, initial encounter
entries.note: Frogs and toads are coded separately, and the committee’s minutes are sealed.

entries.description: Bitten or stung by nonvenomous insect and other nonvenomous arthropods, initial encounter
entries.note: Every nonvenomous insect and arthropod in the world, in one code. The classification believes in economies of scale.

entries.description: Contact with nonvenomous plant thorns and spines and sharp leaves, initial encounter
entries.note: Roses, cacti and holly share a code. The florist has no comment.
The lamppost was not at fault and is not in network.
Subsequent encounter. The lamppost has not moved.
The wall reported no injuries and filed no claim.
Please specify the furniture. The classification declines to.

entries.description: Striking against or struck by other objects, initial encounter
entries.note: The classification’s way of admitting it has run out of nouns.

entries.description: Contact with edge of stiff paper, initial encounter
entries.note: The only paperwork injury with its own code.
Not the kind of needle that comes with a prior authorization.
Running with them is a separate lecture, not a separate code.
See also W26.2XXA, the smaller paperwork incident.

entries.description: Fall from (out of) grocery cart, initial encounter
entries.note: Yes, there is a code for falling out of a grocery cart. No, there is no code for the appeal.

entries.description: Struck by golf ball, initial encounter
entries.note: ‘Fore’ is not a billable modifier.

entries.description: Struck by golf club, initial encounter
entries.note: The only code where the doctor is out of the office and the patient knows why.

entries.description: Struck by soccer ball, initial encounter
entries.note: The beautiful game now has a code, and a deductible.
Yes, there is a code for the X-ray. No, there is no code for the bill.

entries.description: Exposure to other noise, initial encounter
entries.note: Suspected source: the payer’s hold music.

entries.description: Exposure to residence or prolonged visit at high altitude, initial encounter
entries.note: The only code that places the patient above the paperwork.

entries.description: Exposure to sudden change in air pressure in aircraft during ascent, initial encounter
entries.note: Airplane ears have a code. Airline delays do not.

entries.description: Explosion of bicycle tire, initial encounter
entries.note: The tire’s claim was denied as a pre-existing condition.

entries.description: Ring or other jewelry causing external constriction, initial encounter
entries.note: Solved with a small saw, an apology and a form.

entries.description: Slipping, tripping and stumbling without falling, unspecified, initial encounter
entries.note: A code for an injury that did not happen. See also: a prior authorization that almost was.
The chart says ‘pt fell.’ The patient agrees.
Not to be confused with a fall from department chair, which is called a reorganization.
Not to be confused with a curbside consult, which is free and equally risky.
A broken escalator is just stairs. This code is about the working kind.
Unrelated to decision trees, though both involve branches and a hard landing.

entries.description: Fall on same level from slipping, tripping and stumbling without subsequent striking against object, initial encounter
entries.note: Three verbs, one code. Payers approve of bundling.

entries.description: Exposure to other specified factors, initial encounter
entries.note: The factors are specified nowhere.

entries.description: Fall on and from ladder, initial encounter
entries.note: The career ladder is covered elsewhere (Z56).
Yes, sunlight is an external cause. No, your plan does not cover the sun.

entries.description: Contact with hot drinks, initial encounter
entries.note: Coffee’s contribution to healthcare: a code for spilling it, none for going without.

entries.description: Contact with hot toaster, initial encounter
entries.note: There is a code for the toaster. There is no code for the bread.

entries.description: Contact with hot stove (kitchen), initial encounter
entries.note: No prior authorization is required to learn that the stove is hot.

entries.description: Contact with hot saucepan or skillet, initial encounter
entries.note: Cast iron has a code, and a personality.

entries.description: Contact with hot heating appliances, radiators and pipes, initial encounter
entries.note: The building’s heating has always been either this or nothing.

entries.description: Contact with other heat and hot substances, initial encounter
entries.note: See also: the hospital parking lot in August.

entries.description: Exposure to excessive natural cold, initial encounter
entries.note: Not to be confused with the operating room, where the cold is intentional.
Somewhere, a committee added a code for heelies. The minutes are not public.
Separate codes exist for colliding with a stationary object. The stationary object is unavailable for comment.
The motorized kind has its own code, and its own opinions.
‘Rosebud’ has no diagnostic code.
A triple axel is not a diagnosis, but the fall from one might be.

entries.description: Fall from in-line roller-skates, initial encounter
entries.note: In-line and non-in-line skates have separate codes. The wheels were not consulted.

entries.description: Burn due to water-skis on fire, initial encounter
entries.note: Somebody, at some point, needed this code.

entries.description: Injury to barefoot water-skier, initial encounter
entries.note: The classification distinguishes barefoot from shod. Nobody asked the water.

entries.description: Patient room in hospital as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: The place of occurrence: here. The place of billing: elsewhere.

entries.description: Corridor of hospital as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Also the department, on most evenings.

entries.description: Cafeteria of hospital as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: The sandwich is not an external cause. Yet.

entries.description: Operating room of hospital as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Where the time-out happens, and where the schedule argues with it.

entries.description: Other place in hospital as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: The code for wherever the map doesn’t show.

entries.description: Unspecified place in hospital as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Where you are when the sign says ‘you are here’ and you are not.

entries.description: Ambulatory surgery center as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Where surgery is done without an overnight stay, and the paperwork stays over.

entries.description: Health care provider office as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: The place where the co-pay lives.

entries.description: Other ambulatory health services establishments as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Urgent care, presumably, and somewhere, a very long line.

entries.description: Library as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Silence requested, unlike the hold music (W42.9XXA).

entries.description: Post office as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Where ‘the check is in the mail’ becomes a place.

entries.description: Courthouse as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Where the appeal ends up, eventually.

entries.description: Art Gallery as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Injuries caused by the art are classified as critical reviews.

entries.description: Museum as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Do not touch, said the sign. The classification agreed.

entries.description: Music hall as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Coded as a place of occurrence. The occurrence was probably the encore.

entries.description: Opera house as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: A place of occurrence with better documentation than most encounters: three acts and a libretto.

entries.description: Theater (live) as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Coded here when ‘break a leg’ is taken literally.

entries.description: Movie house or cinema as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Coming soon: your prior authorization.

entries.description: Tennis court as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Love, fifteen, thirty, deductible.

entries.description: Squash court as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: A vegetable in the kitchen and a sport here. Coders keep them apart.

entries.description: Parking lot as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Where the visit begins and the patience ends.

entries.description: Bank as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Where the deductible is kept and the co-pay is withdrawn.

entries.description: Supermarket, store or market as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Where the pharmacy hides.

entries.description: Airport as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Boarding time: unspecified. Prior authorization time: also unspecified.

entries.description: Barn as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: A place of occurrence with better ventilation than the average waiting room.

entries.description: Chicken coop as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: The coop has its own code. The rooster’s testimony has not been entered.

entries.description: Farm field as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Coded as a place. The crop is a separate matter, and a subsidy.

entries.description: Amusement park as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: The only place that posts its wait time in advance.

entries.description: Campsite as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: The only place in the classification where ‘no signal’ is a feature.

entries.description: Zoological garden (Zoo) as the place of occurrence of the external cause
entries.note: Where every animal is properly labeled. Unlike the formulary.
The code for ‘not applicable’. Applicable, in practice, to most forms.
Sleeping is an activity. Every clinician is encouraged to try it. None can bill for it.
Watching is an activity. The classification agrees it is tiring.
Horseplay is classified. Horses are not required.
The role in which everyone else is wrong. Compare: the utilization reviewer.
The activity that now occupies most of a clinical day. Not billable, but present.

entries.description: Activity, hand held interactive electronic device
entries.note: The phone. The hold music has its own code (W42.9XXA).

entries.description: Activity, other involving computer technology and electronic devices
entries.note: The patient portal is in here somewhere.
A purl-ous pastime, and a code.
Like suturing, but the thread is not itemized.
The classification says nothing about the missing screw.
Ironing is an activity. Wrinkled scrubs are a lifestyle.
See also: wet floor sign, absent.
Also the process of moving a record from one EHR to another. Some things do not survive the move.
An activity done at home every day, reimbursed at a rate of zero.
The person is lifted. The system, so far, is not.

entries.description: Activity, food preparation and clean up
entries.note: Clean-up, as usual, is part of the activity.
The only code where smoking is encouraged.
Every recipe has a step that says ‘to taste’. Every form has one that says ‘other’.
A leading cause of Saturdays.
The tomatoes are not reimbursed either.
The permit was approved faster than the prior authorization.
Ups, downs and sudden stops. Also known as the claims process.
Eighty-eight keys, one code. Efficiency the payer should try.

entries.description: Activity, drum and other percussion instrument playing
entries.note: Percussion is also a physical exam technique. Only one of them is reimbursed.
Strings attached: also known as the fine print.
The animal remains uncoded, and unfazed.
Milking an animal is an activity. Milking a claim is an art.

entries.description: Activity, grooming and shearing an animal
entries.note: Not to be confused with the payer’s ‘haircut’ on your reimbursement.
In the classification, everything outside is ‘other’.
The cheapest treatment in the classification, and the least reimbursed.
Available in 26.2-mile denominations, none of them covered.
The one exercise that keeps you from writing notes at the same time.
The only place where nobody can page you.

entries.description: Activity, water skiing and wake boarding
entries.note: See also V91.07XA, in which the water-skis are on fire.
What goes down comes back up, unlike a reimbursement.
Two-step is a dance. Two-step authentication is a different code entirely.
Flexible in ways the formulary is not.
Where a great deal of health policy is not decided, but discussed, at length, on the fourth hole.
Strikes, spares and the occasional gutter claim.

entries.description: Activity, physical games generally associated with school recess, summer camp and children
entries.note: Tag, you’re it, and so is your deductible.
See also: contract negotiations with the payer.
A sport in which each side attempts to pin the other. Compare: the appeals process.
The ultimate outcome is not a diagnosis.
A discipline of controlled conflict. Compare: peer-to-peer review.

entries.description: Activity, exercise machines primarily for cardiorespiratory conditioning
entries.note: The treadmill: a machine that goes nowhere while the billing continues.
Step exercise is a workout. Step therapy is a payer requirement. Both are tiring.
Also known as a health plan’s formulary, but shorter.
The only free thing in the classification.
Both ‘other’ and ‘specified’. A contradiction, but a billable one.
The most honest code in the classification.

entries.description: Civilian activity done for income or pay
entries.note: Compare: documentation, which is done for neither.
The category for the work nobody is paid to do, including the forms.
Reserved for activities done for neither pay nor prestige. Podcasts, we suspect.
Everyone’s, most days.

entries.description: Other waiting period for investigation and treatment
entries.note: The official code for waiting. Prior authorization is a subset.

entries.description: Unavailability and inaccessibility of health-care facilities
entries.note: The only diagnosis whose cure is a budget.

entries.description: Unavailability and inaccessibility of other helping agencies
entries.note: Also known as ‘your call is important to us’.

entries.description: Person awaiting admission to adequate facility elsewhere
entries.note: Elsewhere is where all the beds are.

entries.description: Medical services not available in home
entries.note: House calls: not available in the home, only on the phone.

entries.description: Other problems related to medical facilities and other health care
entries.note: The code for whatever the system did that no other code could describe.

entries.description: Unspecified problem related to medical facilities and other health care
entries.note: The patient’s review of the visit, in code.

entries.description: Encounter for issue of repeat prescription
entries.note: A visit whose entire purpose is to re-request permission you already had.
The only code for someone who is not sick and still has to wait.
A person in a bed with nowhere else to go. Familiar to every emergency department.

entries.description: Persons encountering health services in other specified circumstances
entries.note: Anyone, anywhere, for any reason. ‘Specified’ is generous.
To establish that you were healthy before the job did what jobs do.

entries.description: Encounter for examination for insurance purposes
entries.note: The insurer examines you so it can know you better than you do.

entries.description: Encounter for issue of other medical certificate
entries.note: A letter stating what everyone already knew, with a signature.
Diagnosis: form. Prognosis: further forms.

entries.description: Procedure and treatment not carried out due to patient leaving prior to being seen by health care provider
entries.note: Coded as the patient’s decision. The wait behind it rarely gets a code (see Z75.2).

entries.description: Laparoscopic surgical procedure converted to open procedure
entries.note: The prior authorization was for the other one.

entries.description: Procedure and treatment not carried out, unspecified reason
entries.note: The operating schedule, in one line.
There is a code for the patient’s literacy. There is none for the discharge instructions.
A code the profession has been applying to itself for decades.
Peer-to-peer review, but internal.
A phrase that could describe the EHR.

entries.description: Other physical and mental strain related to work
entries.note: A category most clinicians will find covers the whole shift.
Burn-out has a diagnosis code. The staffing plan does not.
Recorded in the chart at 11 p.m. by the clinician, who is on call.
‘Elsewhere’ being the rest of the classification, apparently.

entries.description: Problem related to life management difficulty, unspecified
entries.note: The human condition, coded as such.
Also known as residency.
See also: the hospital cafeteria (Y92.233).
Also known as open enrollment.

entries.description: Person encountering health services to consult on behalf of another person
entries.note: A caregiver: the actual medical system.

entries.description: Person with feared health complaint in whom no diagnosis is made
entries.note: Nothing found. Something billed.

entries.description: Person consulting for explanation of examination or test findings
entries.note: The portal released the results before the doctor could. This is the follow-up.
For the child who ages out of one set of forms and into another.
Specified in the chart, not here.
Yes, it is coded. No, it is not preventable, and the sequelae appear at holiday dinners.
Refill authorizations renew on a schedule, like a subscription nobody wanted.

entries.description: Dependence on other enabling machines and devices
entries.note: The fax machine, disproportionately.

entries.description: Encounter for general adult medical examination without abnormal findings
entries.note: Nothing wrong found. Good news, clinically. Neutral news, financially.

entries.description: Encounter for general adult medical examination with abnormal findings
entries.note: Found something at your free checkup? The checkup stays free. Following up on the finding may not.

entries.description: Encounter for observation for other suspected diseases and conditions ruled out
entries.note: Ruled out: the best possible diagnosis, and the one that reimburses least.

entries.description: Encounter for follow-up examination after completed treatment for conditions other than malignant neoplasm
entries.note: ‘Completed treatment’ is an aspiration, and now a diagnosis.
The diagnosis of last resort and first triage.
A symptom shared by patients, clinicians and the person reading the coding manual.
Also the state of anyone who has reached the payer’s phone tree.
A symptom in patients. A service level in payers.
A symptom, and a staff survey result.
The chart says ‘ouch’. The classification agrees.
When the patient says ‘I just don’t feel right’ and the classification says ‘same’.
From the French for ‘discomfort’, also a fair description of the claims portal.

entries.description: Unilateral inguinal hernia, without obstruction or gangrene, not specified as recurrent
entries.note: The subject of a fictional peace conference on this show. The treaty is still not ratified.

entries.description: Bilateral inguinal hernia, without obstruction or gangrene, not specified as recurrent
entries.note: Two sides, one negotiating table.

entries.description: Unilateral inguinal hernia, without obstruction or gangrene, recurrent
entries.note: Returns, like a denied claim.

entries.description: Calculus of gallbladder without cholecystitis without obstruction
entries.note: The show covers gallbladder surgery as a football game, which the classification does not.
McBurney’s point is the sign. This is the code. The paperwork is another matter.
